rationale: Salsa20 is a stream cipher dominated by a small number of extremely hot ARX (add-rotate-XOR) kernels, so the priority is data-path obfuscation with near-zero per-operation overhead: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain weight because instruction substitution directly obscures the arithmetic identities of the quarter-round while costing almost nothing in speed or size, and SPLIT is weighted strongly as a nearly free diversifier of basic-block structure. FLA receives a solid weight to disrupt the control-flow graph and hinder pattern-matching of the cipher rounds, but its RuntimeCost is held moderate since any dispatcher overhead lands directly in the hot encryption loop. BCF is deliberately de-emphasized (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost) because bogus predicate evaluation multiplies the cost of tight loops for marginal added security on code this small. IBR is kept at a moderate weight for branch hiding in less critical regions, while ICALL is restrained — indirect calls would defeat inlining of the quarter-rounds and carry the highest CorrectnessRisk — and IGV stays modest since the benchmark exposes little global state (static profile shows no source lines or large functions to exploit), making static-data obfuscation low-yield. Overall the table biases the selector toward cheap, high-security-gain transformations and away from expensive control-flow inflation, preserving correctness and acceptable performance for a cryptographic kernel.
